question: Does the publication-mediated Zheng Zhenduo-to-Xu Senyu letter route add a distinct priced-acquisition chronology control for the Tieqin Tongjianlou collection without collapsing it into the 1950-01-29 Deng Zhicheng transaction or binding NLC target catalog numbers 3482/3483?
answer: Yes, at the chronology-firewall level only. A Tsinghua Alumni Association article reproduces a Zheng Zhenduo letter whose year is not written on the surviving letter as described there; the article contextually reconstructs the letter as early 1952 from the Three-Anti campaign context and a contemporaneous Xie Zhiliu report. In a February 18 added note, the reproduced text says that in the previous year the bureau bought two batches of Tieqin Tongjianlou rare books, totaling two hundred million yuan in the then-current currency. The National Library of China 2024 bibliography independently identifies the published letter corpus as Liu Xiangchun, Zheng Zhenduo zhi Xu Senyu hanzha, Lishi Wenxian vol.16, Shanghai Guji Chubanshe, 2012, pp.284-343. The exact target letter page inside that range and the original manuscript image have not been directly reviewed. Therefore the evidence supports a distinct later multi-batch priced-acquisition control conditional on the article's 1952 contextual dating, but does not identify either batch's contents, bind 3482/3483, select the target Tonghu/Zhunzhai transfer mode, or alter any chart rule.
